summary.text: The Age of Discovery, roughly 1418 to 1620 and also called the Age of Exploration, was when European seafarers explored, colonized and conquered regions across the globe.
It connected previously isolated parts of the world into a world-system and laid the groundwork for globalization, spurring international trade.
Portuguese and Spaniards led the way, with Vasco da Gama's sea route to India for Portugal and the voyages of Columbus and Magellan for Spain.

facts.label: Route to India
facts.value: Opened by Vasco da Gama in 1498

facts.label: Magellan expedition
facts.value: 1519 to 1522, opening a route from Atlantic to Pacific

facts.label: Manila galleon
facts.value: A trade route linking the Americas and Asia across the Pacific

facts.label: Columbian exchange
facts.value: Plants, animals, people and diseases moved between hemispheres

items.prompt: Compare a European map from early in the era with one from its end. What change in how the continents were drawn would you see?

options.label: They were redrawn as circles around the Mediterranean
They grew from abstract blobs into outlines more recognizable to us
They shrank as mapmakers removed unexplored regions
They stayed the same but gained more colorful borders

items.explain: The era involved mapping the world, and the continents drawn by European mapmakers developed from abstract blobs into more recognizable outlines.

items.prompt: A visitor says Europeans "discovered" lands where people already lived. Why do many Indigenous peoples challenge that word?

options.label: It treats colonial claiming of their lands as valid and erases their presence
It gives too much credit to the sailors who made the maps
It suggests the lands were empty of any plants or animals
It ignores the role of the Church in organizing voyages

items.explain: Many indigenous peoples have challenged colonial claiming of "discovery" over their lands as forced and negating indigenous presence; the word also implies uncovering what already existed.

items.prompt: Two rival crowns each wanted the riches of the East Indies. How did their paths differ?

options.label: Portugal sailed west across the Atlantic, while Spain went around Africa
Both crowns sent their ships through the same route around Africa
Portugal sailed around Africa to India, while Spain's Columbus sailed west across the Atlantic
Spain sailed overland to India, while Portugal sailed the Pacific

items.explain: A Portuguese expedition under Vasco da Gama reached India by sailing around Africa, while the Spanish funded Columbus's plan to sail west across the Atlantic.

items.prompt: Ships crossing the Atlantic carried more than gold and spices. What happened to some populations in the Americas?

options.label: Local populations grew rapidly because of imported medicine
Their numbers stayed steady as trade routes stayed closed
Their numbers fell only because of changes in the weather
New diseases spread and caused rapid declines in some populations

items.explain: The spread of new diseases, especially affecting American Indians, led to rapid declines in some populations.

items.prompt: A shipment of goods crosses the world in days. Where do the origins of this connected economy lie?

options.label: In the expansion of trade networks during this era of sea voyages
In the factories of the later 19th century alone
In the Roman roads that linked the ancient world
In the rise of the first banking houses in Italy

items.explain: The interconnected global economy of the 21st century has its origins in the expansion of trade networks during this era.

items.prompt: Spain wanted to tie its American holdings to Asia across the Pacific. Which route did that?

options.label: The Treaty of Tordesillas line
The Manila galleon trade route
Vasco da Gama's route around Africa
The Atlantic crossing of Columbus

items.explain: The Manila galleon trade route linked the Americas and Asia across the Pacific.
